messages.author: b8d025f1c60d2466
messages.subject: Removing outliers in geom_boxplot
parts:
Dear list—

I would like to know if there is a way of definitely removing outliers
generated by geom_boxplot. As I see it from the documentation, one can
manipulate the colour, size and shape of outliers but not exclude them
entirely. This is particularly relevant of you add a geom_jitter
layer, as the outliers plotted by geom_boxplot would then be
represented twice (as seems to be the case in the third plot in the
examples in http://had.co.nz/ggplot2/geom_boxplot.html). A workaround
I've found is to set the oultier.size flag to 0, is anyone aware of a
better option?
Also, how do I remove the legend automatically produced by geom_boxplot?

Thanking you in advance,
—Gil

messages.author: 936ef8c6d12fc338
messages.subject: RE: Removing outliers in geom_boxplot
parts:
Dear Gil,

When I combine boxplots and jitter, I set the size of the jitter point smaller than the boxplot outliers and give them another colour. That allows the reader to see the difference between the outliers and the jittered points.

library(ggplot2)
dataset <- data.frame(junk = rnorm(3000, mean = rep(1:3, 100)), x = factor(rep(1:3, 100)))
ggplot(dataset, aes(x = x, y = junk)) + geom_boxplot() + geom_jitter(colour = "red", size = 1)

HTH,

Thierry

messages.subject: Re: Removing outliers in geom_boxplot
parts:
Bedankt Thierry. That's quite an elegant solution when you have a
dense cloud of points to jitter in each boxplot. But that is not my
case unfortunately, so I'll have to consider whether to retain the
outliers or just dump them with oultier.size = 0. Also, I found out
how to remove the legend of the plot:

+ opts (legend.position = "none")

cheers,
—Gil
